source.version: Oregon State Ecampus Research Unit, Research Fellows white paper dated April 2025 (23-page PDF including Appendices 1-3)
source.title_on_document: A New Muse: How Guided AI Use Impacts Creativity in Online Creative Writing Courses

supplement.where: Appendices 1-3 in this PDF (pp. 20-22). The p. 6 cross-reference calls the reflection assignment Appendix 2 and the survey Appendix 3; the actual appendix headings number them 1 and 2.
supplement.holds: Appendix 1 reproduces the student reflection assignment (p. 20); Appendix 2 reproduces the participant survey (p. 21). Appendix 3 gives the consensus creativity score for each of the 31 participants in all three conditions (p. 22), providing participant-level scores absent from the main text.

paper_design_summary: Students in two online sections of an introductory fiction-writing course at Oregon State University each wrote a scene to the same basic prompt three times: without ChatGPT (Week 7), with ChatGPT and no instructor guidance (Week 8), and with ChatGPT after three instructor video lessons and a quiz. All 31 students with three samples are analyzed (40 consented, 9 dropped for a missing sample). Two expert judges gave each of the 93 samples a consensus creativity score from 1 to 7 (Consensual Assessment Technique), and a repeated-measures ANOVA compares the three conditions.

studies.label: Within-subjects course study (three writing conditions, fixed order)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No assignment: every participant did all three conditions in a fixed sequence (no ChatGPT in Week 7, ChatGPT alone in Week 8, ChatGPT with instructor support after video lessons). The paper randomized only the order in which judges saw the samples.
assignment.quote: The exercise in the first condition occurred in Week 7 ... The exercise in the second condition occurred in Week 8 ... The exercise in the second experimental condition came after three video lessons and a quiz.
assignment.locator: p. 6, Pedagogical Approaches to Instructor Scaffolding (Conditions 1-3); p. 5, Data Collection and Table 1

arms.name: Condition 2: ChatGPT without instructor support
arms.description: Writing product with ChatGPT but no instructor scaffolding (Week 8)

arms.name: Condition 3: ChatGPT with instructor support
arms.description: Writing product with ChatGPT after three instructor video lessons and a 10-question quiz

participants.exclusions: Nine of the 40 consenting students were excluded because they did not submit a writing sample in at least one condition. The remaining 31 participants had complete data, totaling 93 writing samples (p. 5, Participant Recruitment; p. 8, Exploratory Data Analysis).
participants.who: Students in two online sections of WR 224 (Introduction to Fiction Writing) at Oregon State University, Spring 2024 (22 and 24 enrolled; 40 consented; 9 removed for a missing sample in at least one condition)
participants.quote: While 40 students consented, a rate of approximately 87%, nine did not submit a writing sample in at least one condition. ... these students were removed, creating a final pool of 31 participants and 93 writing samples.
participants.locator: pp. 4-5, Participant Recruitment; p. 8, Exploratory Data Analysis; p. 5, Table 1 (n = 31 per condition)

ai_tool.how_used: Condition 2: students created an account and used ChatGPT freely to help with the prompt. Condition 3: students used ChatGPT to brainstorm before writing and to identify places to improve afterward, taking its suggestions but not its writing, as modeled in instructor video lessons; 10 suggested prompts were supplied.

task.description: Write a fiction scene about a character at work on the day an unusual incident happens (same basic prompt in all three conditions)

contrasts.reported: Table 3 (ns = 31 per condition): Baseline (1) mean 3.61, SD 1.20, SE 0.22; ChatGPT (2) mean 3.52, SD 0.77, SE 0.14. Table 5 reports Baseline (1) minus ChatGPT (2), i.e. control minus treatment: mean difference 0.01, SE 0.26, t = 0.37, Bonferroni-adjusted p = 1.00, Cohen's D = 0.09. Omnibus repeated-measures ANOVA across all three conditions: F(2, 60) = 5.01, p = .01, eta2 = 0.14 (Table 4). As printed, the 0.01 difference does not equal 3.61 - 3.52, and Table 6 totals (3.88, 3.55, 4.34) differ from Table 3. The printed values are retained.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Table 3; p. 9, Table 4 and Table 5; p. 10, Table 6

contrasts.reported: Table 3 (ns = 31 per condition): ChatGPT + Instructor (3) mean 4.32, SD 1.33, SE 0.24; Baseline (1) mean 3.61, SD 1.20, SE 0.22. Table 5 reports Baseline (1) minus ChatGPT + Instructor (3), i.e. control minus treatment: mean difference -0.71, SE 0.28, t = -2.51, Bonferroni-adjusted p = .05, Cohen's D = 0.63. The Condition Differences text describes this difference as significant; the treatment mean is higher. Signs are retained as printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Table 3; p. 9, Condition Differences and Table 5

contrasts.reported: Table 3 (ns = 31 per condition): ChatGPT + Instructor (3) mean 4.32, SD 1.33, SE 0.24; ChatGPT (2) mean 3.52, SD 0.77, SE 0.14. Table 5 reports ChatGPT (2) minus ChatGPT + Instructor (3), i.e. control minus treatment: mean difference -0.81, SE 0.29, t = -2.81, Bonferroni-adjusted p = .03, Cohen's D = 0.72. The Condition Differences text describes this difference as significant; the treatment mean is higher. Signs are retained as printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Table 3; p. 9, Condition Differences and Table 5

eligibility.reason: 31 people analyzed (all three conditions; 40 consented, 9 removed), well below 50. Conditions ran in a fixed order (Week 7 no AI, Week 8 ChatGPT, then ChatGPT after video lessons), so order was not randomized and criterion 1 also fails. Outcome is an expert CAT creativity score on the writing. Non-random within-person comparison: quasi_people, which the codebook folds into observational context; listed in the screening report as a small non-randomized study.

one_line_finding: Among 31 online fiction-writing students, mean expert creativity was 3.61 without ChatGPT, 3.52 with ChatGPT alone (post hoc p = 1.00), and 4.32 with ChatGPT after instructor lessons (p = .05 vs baseline, p = .03 vs ChatGPT alone, Bonferroni) (pp. 8-9, Tables 3 and 5).
